Court No. - 4 HON'BLE AJIT KUMAR, J.
HON'BLE SWARUPAMA CHATURVEDI, J.
Per Swarupama Chaturvedi,J.

1. Heard Shri Sanjay Kr. Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Harshita Rani,
learned panel counsel for the respondents.
2.

By means of this petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution, the petitioner seeks direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents particularly respondent nos.2 & 3 through Intjar vs Union Of India And 2 Others on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41387461/
2 respondent no.1 to recommend the case of petitioner to Embassy of India in Kuwait for re-issue/renewal of his passport for further period of 10 years.
3.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioners passport was issued on 07.06.2016,
with its validity up to 06.06.2026.
Subsequently, petitioner got implicated in Case Crime No. 138 of 2023, registered under Sections 147, 376, 377, 420, 323, 506, and 406 of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that other members of the petitioners family were also implicated in the same First Information Report and except for the petitioners, the remaining co-accused persons had earlier challenged the FIR by filing Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 11216 of 2023, in which an interim order was passed on 27.07.2023 protecting them.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 11216 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
However, the said writ petition was subsequently dismissed for want of prosecution by order dated 10.01.2024.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that in the meantime, petitioner left India and proceeded to the State of Kuwait.
Subsequently, the petitioner was charge-sheeted in Case Crime No. 138 of 2023 under Sections 376, 377, 420, 506, and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, vide charge sheet dated 29.06.2024.
It is admitted that cognizance and summoning orders were passed on 21.11.2024, and non-bailable warrants have been issued against the petitioner.

It is also submitted that, on account of the petitioners absconding in the aforesaid case, another FIR, being Case Crime No. 32 of 2024 under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code, was registered on 14.02.2024 at the same police station, in which a charge sheet has also been submitted on 30.06.2024 and the matter is pending before the trial court.
5. Learned counsel further submits that upon learning about the issuance of non-bailable warrants in the aforesaid cases, the petitioner intends to return to India to appear before the trial court.
He also submits that the petitioner applied for re-issue/renewal of his passport on 02.07.2025 before the Embassy of India, Kuwait, seeking renewal for a further period of ten years.
The said application was registered as Application Registration No. [ARN] 25-2003350848.

Afterwards, petitioner received a communication dated 24.07.2025 from the Embassy of India, Kuwait, calling for an explanation regarding his involvement in Case Crime No. 138 of 2023 and further directing him to submit either a case closure order or permission from the competent court in compliance of legal requirements, which are mandatory for re-issue of the passport during the pendency of the criminal proceedings.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that it is neither proper, nor justified for the authorities to require the petitioner to submit the letter/objection issued to him, particularly when he is residing outside India and has applied for the re-issuance and renewal of his passport solely to appear in the criminal case.
7. The matter was heard on 13.10.2025, when this Court granted time to learned counsel for the respondents to obtain instructions in the matter.
Afterwards, the matter was heard today, during which learned counsel for the respondents obtained the instruction in the matter and placed before us, which is taken on record.
Learned counsel for the respondent submits that the petitioner did not disclose the details of the pending criminal cases in his passport application and suppressed all information relating thereto.

sentences.text:
3 8. Learned counsel for the respondents has further relied upon the notification of the Ministry of External Affairs dated 25.08.1993 as under :
3.

As per Gazette of India, Ministry of External Affairs's Notification No. GSR 570(E)
dated 25.08.1993 read with Section 22 and Section 6 of the Passports Act, 1967, the citizens of India against whom proceedings in respect of an offence alleged to have been committed by them are pending before a criminal court in India, passport facility cannot be rendered to them under section 6(2) (f) of the Passports Act, 1967 unless they produce orders from the court concerned permitting them to depart from India.

9. Relying upon relevant provisions of the Passport Act, Rules and notifications, she further submitted that applicant is required to submit proper explanation/ clarification regarding suppression of pending criminal cases in his passport application and also require to produce the order/ no objection certificate from the Court concerned permitting him to travel abroad in terms of notification no. GSR 570(E) dated 25.08.1993.

Learned counsel further submits that, based on the instructions received, the petitioners passport application is currently on hold at the Embassy of India, Kuwait, and that the application can be processed once the petitioner completes all requirements, including obtaining an order from the competent Court having necessary permission in terms of the Notification dated 25.08.1993.

10. After perusal of the records and in light of the statutory provisions, as well as the legal principles established by various Courts, it is evident that the requirement of obtaining permission from the competent Court to travel abroad is intended to ensure that the trial is not delayed due to the absence of the accused.

11. It is an admitted fact in the present case that the petitioner left India while the trial was pending,
which has not only caused a delay in the proceedings but also led to the issuance of non-bailable warrants against him.
The records further reveal that the petitioners passport remains valid until 06.06.2026.

We are of the considered view that the petitioner may, therefore, travel to India to appear before the competent Court and to participate in the trial, and obtain the requisite permission from the Court to travel abroad.
Thereafter, he may comply with the requirements of Notification dated 25.08.1993 and pursue the re-issuance of his passport with the authorities.

12. We are also of the considered view that, even in circumstances where the validity of a passport has expired, Section 4(2)(a) of the Passport Act, 1967, empowers the Government to issue an Emergency Certificate to facilitate the return of an individual to India.
While the petitioners passport remains valid in the present case, this provision ensures that no person is prevented from returning to the country due to the expiry of a passport.

Accordingly, in the event of a future lapse of passports validity, petitioner would still be entitled to return to India and thereafter comply with all procedural requirements for re-issuance or renewal of the passport.

13. After due consideration of the submissions and record, and in accordance with the principles laid down in Rahimuddin v. Union of India & Another, 2025 SCC OnLine All 6964 (Neutral Citation No.
Intjar vs Union Of India And 2 Others on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41387461/
4 2025:AHC:181505-DB), we are of the considered view that petitioner in the first instance should apply for emergency certificate before Indian Embassy in Kuwait and if he does so, his application for such a certificate may be considered and disposed of expeditiously.

14. We further provide that in the event petitioner gets emergency certificate to travel back to India,
he upon coming shall in the first instance appear before the trial Court to meet non-bailable warrant, if any and then shall obtain necessary no objection/ approval/ sanction to travel abroad and his application for no objection and his application for re-issuance of passport shall be disposed of in consonance with the observations and directions rendered in Rahimuddin v. Union of India &
Another (supra).
15.
